description: The National Performance of Dams Program at Stanford University collects information on dam incidents and failures in the United States and publishes it through a database, a digital library and a dam dictionary. The home page lists specialty databases on dams and earthquakes, penstock incidents, a geomembrane database built with CARPI, a post-tension anchor database and incidents at hydropower projects, plus resources such as Dam Failures in the U.S. (NPDP-01 V1), life-safety consequences of dam failures, and a report on developing F-N curves for public safety risk from dam failures. It also carries a perspective on viewing a dam as a system of structures, reservoir, mechanical and electrical parts and operators, a form to report a dam incident, and the 2017 Oroville spillway forensic team report. Coverage: United States dams, incident-level. Access: free web resources; the licence is not stated on the page read, and the database query pages themselves were not opened. Caveats: the incident record relies on voluntary reporting; this record is based on the home page. It provides failure frequencies and consequence data for dam breach, cascading failure and risk-to-life simulations, and relates to the ASDSO incident database and the Oroville forensic record in the catalogue.
